title: When the Safehouse Falls
premise: Beatrix Hartwell, a whistle-blower who has lived under four names in seven years, discovers her safehouse listed for sale online — with interior photos that reveal her hiding places, her routines, and her face. The listing is bait, and the trap is an attack planned to look like a gas accident during the Geneva summit. Forced out of hiding and into an uneasy alliance with the handler who betrayed her and the young analyst who found the listing, Beatrix must decide who she is when every name is burned. In the end she stops the attack by going public with the evidence she once buried, trading anonymity for belonging — and finally choosing one name as her own.
about_author: W. M. Whitlock is the pen name of a former intelligence-community contractor who writes thrillers about people erased by the systems they served. Whitlock lives under no particular name in a coastal town where everyone knows everyone's business.

chapters.title: Four Names on the Door
chapters.summary: Beatrix Hartwell's POV. A quiet morning in the Rotterdam safehouse establishes her rules: no photos, no patterns, no real names. She almost relaxes over coffee with neighbor Marta, the closest thing to a friend she's allowed herself. Emotional beat: fragile contentment built on denial.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Beatrix finds her safehouse for sale online — twelve interior photos including her hidden document cache behind the wardrobe. POV shifts to Elias Voss, her former handler, receiving the same link from an unknown sender. Emotional beat: cold dread; the walls of her life were never hers.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: Beatrix runs, following protocol, but every fallback contact is dead or compromised. Flashbacks reveal the leak she exposed seven years ago at Halcyon Logistics. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being the only person who remembers the truth.

chapters.title: The Analyst
chapters.summary: Introduce Priya Nair, a junior OSINT analyst who flagged the listing's metadata and can't let it go. Her POV shows institutional rot at the agency meant to protect assets like Beatrix. Emotional beat: idealism colliding with complicity.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Beatrix breaks her own rule and approaches Priya, betting the enemy expects her to run, not investigate. Their tense first meeting in a tram depot; Priya proves the listing was posted from inside the protection program. Emotional beat: wary first trust.

chapters.title: Voss Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Elias intercepts them both, claiming he's trying to find who sold Beatrix out before the program's own cleaners do. Beatrix doesn't believe him; he knows too much anyway. Emotional beat: hatred and dependence braided together.

chapters.title: What the Photos Show
chapters.summary: Priya analyzes the listing photos frame by frame and finds deliberate staging — objects placed to signal someone who knew the safehouse intimately. Only four people ever had access. Emotional beat: betrayal narrowing into a short list.

chapters.title: Marta
chapters.summary: Beatrix returns for Marta and finds her flat searched, Marta gone. Guilt crushes her: proximity to Beatrix is a death sentence. Emotional beat: grief as the price of connection; she vows never again — a vow the story will break.

chapters.title: The Summit Calendar
chapters.summary: Priya connects the timeline: the attack is scheduled during the Geneva energy summit, disguised as infrastructure failure. They realize the target isn't Beatrix — she's the loose end, not the point. Emotional beat: scale shift from personal fear to public stakes.

chapters.title: Halcyon Rises
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter: Beatrix's original whistle-blowing, the documents she buried to survive, and the contract she never finished reading. Present-day Voss admits Halcyon rebuilt itself under new names. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Safehouse Two
chapters.summary: The trio holes up in a derelict canal barge. Found-family dynamics spark: Priya cooks, Voss tells stories, Beatrix resists belonging. Emotional beat: warmth arriving uninvited and unwelcome.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix reveals her three prior identities to Priya — and admits she can't remember which parts of herself are real. Priya argues identity is chosen, not assigned. Emotional beat: the book's thematic heart, spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Inside Man
chapters.summary: Voss identifies the likely traitor: Deputy Director Corliss, who signed off on all four of Beatrix's placements. But the evidence could equally implicate Voss himself. Emotional beat: suspicion poisoning the fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Geneva Bound
chapters.summary: They travel separately to Geneva under new covers Beatrix builds herself — the first identities she authors rather than receives. Surveillance, near-misses, a tail they barely lose. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed through craft.

chapters.title: The Gas Works
chapters.summary: Recon of the summit's backup power facility reveals the staged-accident mechanism: a gas main rerouted to fail catastrophically mid-summit. Beatrix recognizes the engineering signature — Halcyon's. Emotional beat: horror at how neat the murder will look.

chapters.title: Corliss
chapters.summary: Beatrix confronts Corliss at a summit reception wearing a borrowed identity. He offers her reinstatement, a fifth name, everything back — if she walks away. Emotional beat: temptation of erasure versus the cost of witness.

chapters.title: Sold Out Again
chapters.summary: Their barge safehouse is raided; Priya is taken. Beatrix realizes Voss fed Corliss their location to save his own pension — or so it appears. Emotional beat: the found family shatters at its weakest seam.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV in captivity: Corliss tries to turn her with the same logic Beatrix rejected — survival through silence. Priya stalls, leaks a coded message in her interrogation transcript. Emotional beat: courage without experience.

chapters.title: What Voss Buried
chapters.summary: Voss, cornered by Beatrix, confesses: he protected her seven years ago because the buried Halcyon files also incriminate him. He gives her the original cache location. Emotional beat: a betrayer choosing, too late but not too late, to be useful.

chapters.title: Twenty Minutes to Failure
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Beatrix infiltrates the gas works during the summit's opening session while Voss draws security. Sabotage countdown, alarms, a fight on the catwalks above the mains. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Going Loud
chapters.summary: Beatrix stops the physical attack but realizes the paper trail dies with Corliss unless someone testifies. She broadcasts the Halcyon files live, burning every alias forever, as Priya escapes in the chaos and Corliss is arrested mid-denial. Emotional beat: liberation through self-destruction of the old self.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Resolution. Weeks later: hearings underway, Marta found alive, Voss awaiting trial, Priya visiting. Beatrix registers her real name — Beatrix Hartwell, the fourth name, now the only one — and answers her door without checking the peephole. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last.
